title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement:
Given the `head` of a linked list, remove the `n`th node from the end of the list and return its head.

Build the list from `values`, use a dummy node before the head plus two pointers separated by `n` steps so that when the faster pointer reaches the end, the slower pointer sits right before the node to remove, then splice it out. Return the resulting list as an array.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 30]

editorial.approach: Create a dummy node pointing to `head` (handles removing the true head cleanly). Advance a `fast` pointer `n` steps ahead of a `slow` pointer that starts at the dummy. Then move both forward together until `fast` reaches the last node — at that point `slow` is positioned right before the node to remove. Splice it out with `slow.next = slow.next.next` and return `dummy.next`.
editorial.complexity: O(n) time / O(1) extra space (single pass)
